body: Quick pass (UMA) @ c6c658db: reproduced as P0 (a stock-sourced Bore's entry rapid 3 mm into uncut stock, posted with no warning). Quick gate green on the final head + 11 Bore/Thread suites + clippy, no goldens moved, the pin fails without the fix. Flagged ready for an independent review at the effort:high tier (rapid-in-stock law).

<!-- pr-reviewer: c6c658db94ac0757546157e1bab0711af44eb6d1 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** No blockers found. This was a high-tier review: I read the logic adversarially and did not count the existing label or earlier review comments as evidence.

**What I built and ran.** I checked out head `c6c658db` in its own worktree and trial-merged current `origin/main` (`a6bd69d8`). It was already up to date, with no conflicts.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test ladder_entry_height` | 4 passed |
| circular_pick / drill_rplane / golden_cl / level_links / mill2d_c / operations / project_roundtrip / refusal_location (the suites that build stock-sourced Bore or Thread ops) | 4 / 8 / 25 / 7 / 9 / 117 (6 ignored) / 71 / 3 passed, 0 failed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

**What looks good**
- The change is small and covers exactly what the issue reported. `judged_stock` only takes effect when `stock_facets` is `None`, the source is `SrcRef::Stock` and the kind is `Bore` or `Thread`. Every other source and kind still gets `stock_facets` back unchanged, so a model-sourced, selection-sourced or sketch-sourced op reads verify exactly as before.
- The fix touches only verify. `stock_region` is read only by the two `VerifyContext { stock: .. }` sites (generate.rs:2737 and the 3+2 site at 3057), so no generator input moves and no golden changes. golden_cl passes 25/25.
- The heights still come from one place. The rapid's end Z comes from the hole's `entry_z` (the ladder), and the cap still comes from `stock_top_z`. The PR only changes which XY counts as stock, and does not compute a second height.
- In the 3+2 branch, `material.facets` are in world coordinates (the corner loop at generate.rs:3027 reads them that way), so the `f.local_facets(..)` mapping is the same one `stock_facets` already got. Nothing is transformed twice.
- Thread is in the same `matches!` arm. Its descent (`thread_mill.rs:232-240`) is a rapid to `x.top_z`, the hole's mouth, so stock standing above the mouth is now convicted for Thread too. That is correct. A rapid to exactly the mouth stays silent (`m.to.z + lift < surface - z_tol`).
- `acquit_by_prior` still clears a dive into stock that an earlier op removed. This is pinned by the face-ahead test.
- The process items are in place: a `docs/decisions/1066-*.md` file, `Changelog:`, `Fixes #1066`, provenance and a gate map on the new suite, tests in the owning crate, and no process files or snapshot PNGs touched.

**What I tried that held.** I wanted to know whether this could falsely refuse a legal program, so I wrote a local probe (not pushed, now deleted). The stock was a "from model" casting, solid to Z 20 over the hole's mouth with a boss to Z 30 elsewhere, and I ran a stock-sourced and a part-sourced Bore on it. Both gave the same verdict: `RapidInStock { at: 0 }` on the entry dive to Z 22. The column cap is the flat `stock_top_z`, which is the global maximum (30), not the local top over the hole (20). So on a stepped stock the law over-reports. It refuses; it does not gouge.

This behaviour already exists on main for model-sourced Bores, and this PR extends it to stock-sourced Bore and Thread, so it does not block this merge. It may be worth a follow-up issue: "column law caps at the global stock top; a stepped FromModel/carried stock over-reports a dive to a lower mouth". My probe also imported the casting as a model, which added a gouge refusal, so it was not a clean repro of that case alone.

**Questions / notes (not blocking)**
1. `rustfmt --check` would rewrap two new lines (`material_source.rs:344-345` and the `use camcraft_app::commands::{..}` line in the test). This is cosmetic.
2. `generate.rs` was already about 3245 lines. This adds a net +1 line, so I am noting the file's size, not the change.
3. Not exercised, as you said: no Thread pinning test and no tilted (3+2) test. I did not write one either.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
